sentences.text: Brief facts leading to filing of this appeal are that, on 20.09.2014 at about 6:00 hours, the deceased Omkar Pradeep Salunke along with his friends was running on the Kaccha Road situated by the side of the Tar Road from Nippani towards Yamagarnias, as they were practicing running to attend the competition for selection in Military Services.

When the deceased came near Walves Field on NH-4, a NWKRTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-42/F-1468 came behind the deceased in a rash and negligent manner, at high speed without observing the traffic rules and regulations, dashed to the deceased.
Due to the said impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries to vital parts of his body and subsequently 'Tribunal', for short NC: 2024:KHC-D:11430 succumbed to the said injuries.
Hence, the parents of the deceased filed claim petition before the Tribunal claiming compensation.
3. The respondent-Corporation entered appearance and filed an objection statement denying the averments made in the claim petition and sought dismissal of the claim petition.
4. Claimant No.2 examined herself as PW1 and got marked 8 documents as per Exs.P1 to P8.
The respondent- Corporation examined its driver as RW1 and no documents were marked.

The Tribunal on appreciation of the entire material available on record awarded a total compensation of Rs.10,89,000/- with interest at the rate of 9% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
Being aggrieved by the same, the claimants are in appeal seeking higher compensation.

5. Learned counsel Ms. Kavita Rathod appearing on behalf of Shri Santosh B. Malagoudar for the appellants-claimants submits that the Tribunal has NC: 2024:KHC-D:11430 committed an error in considering the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month.

She submits that the deceased was aged about 18 years as on the date of the accident and was doing Goundi Work and earning Rs.
10,000/- per month.

Further, she submits that the Tribunal has not appreciated the pleadings and evidence in a proper perspective and awarded meager compensation for the accidental death of the son of the appellant No.1.
Thus, she seeks to enhance the same appropriately by allowing the appeal.

6. Per contra, learned counsel Sri. C.R. Menasinkai appearing for the respondents-Corporation supports the impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal and submits that the appellants have failed to prove the income of the deceased before the Tribunal and hence, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month.
He further submits that the Tribunal has rightly awarded compensation under each heads and does not call NC: 2024:KHC-D:11430 for any Shri.Pradeep vs The Managing Director

Hence, he seeks for dismissal of the appeal.

7. Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of appeal papers, the only point that would arise for consideration in this appeal is as to whether appellants are entitled for higher compensation?

8. It is not in dispute that in a road traffic accident occurred on 20.09.2024, the deceased-Omkar,
son of the appellants, succumbed to the injuries.
The Tribunal, while determining the compensation has assessed the income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month.
Though the claimants pleaded that the deceased was doing Goundi Work and earning Rs.10,000/- per month.
However, no cogent and legally acceptable evidence was placed on record by the claimants to substantiate the income of the deceased.
In the absence of any cogent evidence to prove the income of the deceased, it is for the Courts to assess the monthly income notionally, taking note of the income chart prepared by the KSLSA.
As per the chart, the notional NC: 2024:KHC-D:11430 income for the year 2014 is Rs.7,500/- per month.
Hence, taking note of the same, this Court reassesses notional income of the deceased at Rs.7,500/- per month.

In terms of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited Vs.Pranay Sethi & Others2, the deceased was aged 18 years as on the date of accident, the claimants would be entitled to an addition of 40% of the assessed income towards loss of future prospects and appropriate multiplier would be 18.

sentences.text: In view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation3, the deduction towards personal and living expenses of the deceased would be 50% of the assessed income as the deceased was a bachelor.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, the claimants would be entitled for modified compensation under the head of "loss of dependency" at Rs.11,34,000/- (Rs.7,500 + 40% - 50% x 12 x 18).
2017(16) SCC 680 2009 ACJ 1298 NC: 2024:KHC-D:11430 9.

Further, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/-
towards funeral expenses and transportation of dead body with 10% escalation.

10. In terms of decision of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Company Limited Vs. Nanu Ram & Others4, each of the appellants- claimants would be entitled to Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of consortium' with 10% escalation.

Loss of dependency Rs.11,34,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.16,500/-
 Funeral expenses  & transportation of dead body Rs.16,500/-
 Loss of consortium  (Rs.40,000/- x 3 + 10%) Rs.1,32,000/-

In the result, this Court proceeds to pass the following:
ORDER (i) Appeal stands partly allowed.
(ii) The impugned judgment and award of the  Tribunal is modified holding that the  claimants are entitled to total  compensation of Rs.12,99,000/- as against Rs.10,89,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.
(iii) The enhanced compensation amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.
(iv) The appellant are not entitled to interest for the delayed period of 384 days in filing this appeal as per the order dated 10.04.2018.
(v) The respondent/Corporation shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
NC: 2024:KHC-D:11430 (vi) The apportionment, deposit and disbursement shall be made in terms of award of the Tribunal.
(vii) Registry to draw modified award accordingly.
(viii) No costs.
